lean.basis: Ran Breitbart News from 2012 and in 2016 called it "the platform for the alt-right"; Trump's 2016 campaign chief and White House chief strategist, now host of War Room. Widely described as a far-right figure; Bannon denies being a white nationalist or antisemitic.

PBS NewsHour: Critics say Bannon in White House would empower fringe voices

current_role: Host of the War Room podcast; former White House chief strategist (2017)
summary: Steve Bannon, a former Navy officer and Goldman Sachs banker, helped found Breitbart News and was a vice president of Cambridge Analytica before running Trump's 2016 campaign and serving as White House chief strategist for seven months in 2017. Since 2019 he has hosted the War Room podcast, a hub of the populist right; he has feuded with Elon Musk and the tech right and promotes an unconstitutional third Trump term. Trump pardoned him on federal fraud charges in 2021; he served four months in 2024 for contempt of Congress and pleaded guilty to a New York fraud charge in 2025.

connections.name: Stephen Miller
connections.description: While working for Sessions, Miller cultivated close ties with Breitbart News under Bannon; leaked emails from 2015–2016 show Miller pitching and shaping Breitbart stories, with Bannon among the editors copied. They worked together in the early Trump White House, and Miller distanced himself from Bannon after Bannon's 2017 exit.

connections.description: Bannon, then Breitbart News executive chairman, tried to recruit Sessions to run for president in 2013, called him a mentor, and is reported to have urged him to endorse Trump in February 2016. Breitbart defended Sessions during his attorney general confirmation.

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: Bannon left Breitbart to become chief executive of Trump's campaign in August 2016 and was White House chief strategist until August 18, 2017. The White House called his exit a mutual decision; other reports said he was pushed out, and Bannon said he had already offered his resignation.

connections.description: The Mercer family co-owned Breitbart News, which Bannon chaired, and largely owned Cambridge Analytica, where Bannon was a board vice president.
